title: Oracle-selection training: each step a dense backward picks the smallest token set holding 0.95 gradient cosine (per document / per row / batch), then the update comes from a forward+backward on that set only; one arm adds 2x random tokens
result: 1,952 rows/task, single cut at block 7, 1 seed, eval_size 500/cell, no-cot; 8k mean, dense 0.843, recipe 0.845). Only per-document allocation survives: per-doc oracle keeps 35% of body tokens, 0.850 (ties dense); per-row 29%, 0.674 (outlier@8k 0.155); batch-global 19%, 0.756 (outlier 0.537); per-doc with two cuts (7+16) 0.716. Picking for 0.95 attribution cos gives only ~0.5-0.6 routed-gradient cos in every arm, and batch/row arms fit their own subset (routed train CE 0.12 vs dense 0.17). Random negatives help: 13% batch oracle + 17% random = 0.806, outlier 0.155 -> 0.737 vs per-row at the same ~30% keep, routed cos 0.74. Costs ~2.3x dense per step, so an upper bound, not a method; it does not beat the recipe. Batch oracle grown until the ROUTED gradient cos reaches 0.95 (orc1batchrc, 71% kept on average, rising 63% -> 77-80% over training; routed cos 0.99): 8k mean 0.837 vs dense 0.843 (contra 0.964, nq 0.912, outlier 0.843, oolong 0.629), 2k 0.936 vs 0.933, so matching the true gradient fixes outlier but needs most tokens. Literal rule (orcbatchall: batch-global, two cuts, cos 0.95 on the WHOLE gradient incl. prompt/query/answer): 8k mean 0.736 (nq 0.894, outlier 0.501, oolong 0.591), 2k mean 0.846 vs dense 0.933 (outlier 0.570 vs 0.911): same failing group as row/batch. Per-doc oracle + 2x random (orc1docr2): 8k 0.867 / 2k 0.933, but it keeps nearly every token, so it is a near-dense control, not a test of negatives. Two-cut batch on body tokens (orcbatch): 8k 0.793. All 9 arms done. Verdict: gradient-faithful token sets need ~70% of the body; the 20%/7% router ties dense through co-adaptation to a stable rule, not gradient matching. Session page https://claude.ai/artifact/9vAYqzh69sXf1RjVFfsnNV. Record records/oracle-selection-training.md, branch claude/oracle-train-bd7414.

title: Gradient maps: per-token x per-layer gradient on frozen checkpoints (log and linear color scales)
result: One dense forward + backward of the answer CE per row on base, dense 1,952 / 7,808 rows/task and the recipe (8k: eval_size 512 rows, 128/task; 2k ⚠ 128 rows, 32/task). Answer + query tokens (2-10% of tokens) carry 60-95% of the blocks 7-31 gradient energy. Gold documents carry 8-55x the energy per token of distractors on nq/contradiction (outlier 2.4-3.8x). Training moves energy to the top layers (block 31 alone 18-48% at 7,808) and distractor energy drops 1-2 orders of magnitude at layers 17-20. Token importance rank-correlates 0.92-0.93 between adjacent layers but 0.57-0.61 for block 7 vs 16 and 0.33-0.39 for 7 vs 31. Linear color scale: the panel max is 1,000-10,000x the 99th percentile, so a trained checkpoint's update is the answer tokens; capped at the 99th percentile, document gradient sits in a few documents (gold + 3-4), in blocks 0-15, on a few tokens. Routed forward (recipe): answer CE close to dense, kept document tokens' ||dL/dh|| 1.6-4x higher above block 7; per-batch routed/dense energy median 1.97 (~1.4x in norm). Figures in the Gradient maps tab.

title: Router ranking accuracy across layers, and gradient magnitude under token drop
result: Ranking: the ridge router ranks tokens with Spearman 0.51-0.67 against its own target (base-model probe ⚠ 32 held-out rows/task; 0.54 / 0.57 at blocks 7 / 16 on the trained recipe). Its top 30% holds 73-95% of the squared gradient (true top 30%: 90-99%, random 30%). Even a perfect block-7 ranker ranks the top layers poorly: true ranking rank-correlates 0.57-0.61 between blocks 7 and 16 and 0.33-0.39 between 7 and 31. Never measured: the trained router's picks against the true gradient at blocks 16/24/31 (its logged rank_corr_explore / rank_corr_kept are in wandb, not pulled). Magnitude: attribution subsets at cos 0.95 keep 91-95% of the gradient norm; in routed training the gradient norm is not smaller (oracle arms 0.81-1.25x dense; recipe ~1.4x per batch), because dropping context raises loss on nearly solved rows.

title: Literature review: efficient long-context training (token dropping, routing, selection, backward compression)
result: ~70 papers through Nov 2026. Mid-stack token dropping in training with dense inference is prior art (Hou 2022 token dropping, Random-LTD; LeMo/Jenga for long-context LoRA fine-tuning). No published long-context fine-tuning method reports more than ~1.4-2x training savings at parity; our ~4-4.5x is above everything found. Fitting a token router online to per-token gradient-norm targets appears novel, but random nearly ties it, so it is a weak headline. Baselines to run: Random-LTD per-layer resampling, attention-score selection at block 7 (LeMo / A-MoD style), an end-to-end MoD / TokenGate-style gate, LongLoRA S2-Attn, and InfoBatch / GRESO-style forward skipping of solved rows (most promising toward 5x+).

title: Aggressive keep trained directly: 10%@7 → 3% or 5%@16 (gradient-gap follow-up)
result: 1 seed, eval_size 500/cell. 10%→3%: 0.860 @293 PF (3.1×) at f1952; 0.909 @585 PF (3.9×) at f3904. 10%→5%: 0.848 @305 (2.4×); 0.909 @608 (3.7×). Recipe: 4.1× / 3.7×. Ties the recipe at f3904, loses at f1952; only 12–15% fewer FLOPs because blocks 0–6 run dense (floor ≈0.2× dense/step). Not a path to ≥5×.

title: Early-phase gradient probe: when does the routed gradient become unbiased?
result: ⚠ eval_size 256/ckpt. Router-routed gradient biased right after step 0 (step 8: exp cos 0.41 Adam, norm 1.6–2.6×), unbiased again by step 31 (0.81) and at 244 (0.88, norm 1.00). Random never recovers (≤0.35). Aggressive budgets (10%@7, 3%@16) on the recipe-trained model peak ~0.7–0.78 at step 31 then decay to ~0.38. Biased phase is short (~6% of training). Branch claude/grad-routing-gap.

title: Gradient sparsity vs routing gap: where the 1–4%-token oracle bound breaks
result: Dense ckpt: attribution 0.996 expected → true routed 0.12 (oracle), 0.04 (router), 0.03 (random); >97% of loss = kept tokens' gradients shifting when context is removed. Recipe ckpt (trained routed): router-routed gradient nearly unbiased (expected cos 0.874 raw/0.831 Adam, norm ratio 0.89; routed CE ≈ dense); random stays biased (0.18). Block-16-only 7% with router: 0.983. Gap to the 11–20× bound likely = early off-distribution phase + block-7 stage. Next: late-split-only training; early-phase probe. Branch claude/grad-routing-gap.

title: Backward compression with exact forward: token-sparse and sketched backward
result: Failed. Row-sparse backward cuts the step to 0.11–0.13× dense (recipe 0.22×) with grad cosine 0.85–0.96, but training CE stalls at ≈0.3 and contradiction/outlier collapse: 8-cell 0.51–0.69 vs recipe 0.883 at f1952, 0.68 vs 0.915 at f3904. Exact backward every 2nd step: 0.810 at 0.158×. Unbiased sketches diverge. Kept: answer-only head (−0.017×/step) and exact zero-row skip (≈3%). Branch claude/sparse-backward.

title: Large-data decay: diagnosis on answer CE + ReLoRA merge-restart and late keep-widening
result: Corrected after 2 seeds: late widening (35/15% last third) at 7,808 rows is within seed noise of the recipe (f1 0.931 vs 0.926, +0.005±≈0.003; CE 0.1404 vs 0.1439, −0.0035±≈0.004; +8.6% FLOPs) and short of dense CE (0.1374). Seed 0's >4.1× was a lucky draw. Decay is mostly dense's ceiling + seed noise; ReLoRA null. Need ≥3 seeds/arm at this scale. Branch claude/tokdrop-decay-fix.

title: Multiple views per row from cached block-7 states
result: Failed. All k>1 runs trail the recipe at matched FLOPs: k=2 −0.013 (f1952) / −0.011 (f3904); k=3 −0.069 / −0.017 (1 seed, eval_size 500/cell). Extra views act like extra epochs; fresh rows are a better use of FLOPs. Branch claude/multiview-h7cache.

title: Brainstorm: 10 ambitious ideas ranked (backward compression, large-data fix, multi-view rows, stochastic early backward, contextual-sparse early MLPs, answer-only LM head, keep schedule, length curriculum, local attention at 64k)
result: Key constraint found: the forward floor is ≈0.10× dense with an exact forward split at block 7, so ≥5× needs the backward (≈half the cost) cut 2–5×. Top 3 launched overnight. Odds: ≈25% to reach ≥5× at small data and ≥3.5× at 7,808 rows; <5% for 10× at large data on this setup.

title: Gradient concentration across training stages: tokens needed for 70 / 90 / 95% of the update, and speedup bounds
result: Preliminary (existing probe, per row, up to 366 steps): signal sharpens by ≈31–61 steps then spreads out; at 366 steps block 16 needs 15% of tokens for 95% (recipe keeps 7%). Full whole-update analysis on fresh checkpoints to 1,952 steps running.

title: Per-layer skipping overhead: token-level vs 100/128-token chunks (microbenchmark)
result: Gather/scatter adds only 1–5% of a full layer per layer at 32k (token 4.7% GDN / 1% attention; 100–128-token chunks ≈2.5% / 1%). The real loss is short sequences: at 8k, keeping 25% makes a GDN block only 30% faster (attention 64%); at 32k time tracks FLOPs. Chunking barely matters for speed. 1 H200 (sneetches), timing noisy at 8k.

title: Recipe on Qwen3-4B (full attention, 36 layers): does it generalize, are gains larger with more attention?
result: Interim (1 seed): generalizes but smaller gain: best split 12/24 gives 2.09× dense FLOPs-to-match at 1,952 rows vs 4.63× on Qwen3.5; same per-row FLOP cut (0.22–0.29×), bigger accuracy loss at matched data (mostly outlier/contra, shrinking with data). LoRA matters here (routing only 1.19×) and is the memory win (19.5 vs 57 GiB). Dense 3,904 / 7,808 pending.

title: Model-scale ablation: dense vs recipe on smaller Qwen3.5 models
result: Gain grows with scale at fixed data: FLOPs-to-match at 1,952 rows 1.73× (0.8B) / 2.42× (2B) / 4.08× (4B) / >4.42× (9B: recipe 0.902/0.903 at 632 PF beats dense 0.900 at 2,792); at 3,904 rows 1.88 / 3.22 / 3.68×. At large data the ratio tracks where dense saturates. Routing, not LoRA, carries the 0.8B crossing. 9B dense at 3,904 pending.

result: Cheap scoring pass picks rows; ceiling 3–5× on top of routing. Screenable on existing fresh pools. Awaiting Prasann's go. Dropped 10-29 (Prasann: no drastic data changes for now).

title: Small-model front end (0.8B picks tokens for the 4B)
result: Cost model only (no training): with a 0.8B selector the ceiling is ≈1.35× over the recipe (≈4× dense) assuming no score loss; even a near-free selector with 7% kept from block 0 is ≈2.6× (≈8× dense) only if score is unchanged. Measured early drops already lose 0.04–0.08, random token choice ≈ router (0.914 vs 0.915), so selection is not the bottleneck: realistic ≈1.9× dense, below the recipe's ≈3×. Branch claude/small-model-select-0a941a (small_model_cost.py).

title: Unified results hub (this page) and experiment log
result: Nine sections with sidebar navigation; detail pages and the Aug–Sep archive linked under Provenance.

title: Layer-skip screen, 44 runs: fixed skips (20/24/28, 20–27), LayerDrop on 16–29, gradient-ranked top-25/50% layers (update-only and forward-skip)
result: Dense + skips ties dense at 0.78–0.89× FLOPs (Δ −0.03 to +0.02); recipe + skip loses 0.007–0.13 for 3–8% FLOPs; forward-skip selectors collapse. Record: records/layer-skip-screen.md (branch claude/train-layerskip-35010b).

title: Fresh-pool FLOP curves for layer-skip arms
result: Not launched: best case ≈1.1–1.2× FLOPs-to-match, far below routing.

title: Hill-climb replicates: adaptive stage-2 budget (3 seeds), MLP + per-group ridge (2 seeds)
result: Adaptive budget 0.864 vs the recipe's 0.852 (+3.5% FLOPs) on the 1,464-row screen; MLP + per-group ridge 0.856, no gain.

title: Scored dense at 5,856 / 7,808 fresh rows and the recipe at 7,808
result: Dense 0.928 / 0.931; the recipe's 0.926 at 7,808 equals dense at 3,904, so FLOPs-to-match ≈2.0× is now a point estimate (good only to ≈1.5–4×: dense is flat there).

title: Frozen-output-layer whole-model LoRA at 64k and 128k (full-row CE)
result: −0.0057 / −0.0039 / −0.0026 at 64k after 120 / 240 / 480 steps; −0.0038 / −0.0046 at 128k after 48 / 120; the 64k 240-step run ties dense at 480 (≈2.9×). 0.68× FLOPs at both lengths.

title: Matched SFT + CTC generation eval of the CPT checkpoints
result: Held for Prasann's decision.

title: LoRA × routing 2×2 ablation (each cell at its best LR)
result: Routing does most of the gain; LoRA-all is 15–35% of it on the 4-task mix and shrinks with data on 11-task (54% → 19% → 7%). At matched data all arms score within ≈0.03: the gain is cheaper steps. Record: records/lora-vs-routing-ablation.md (branch claude/vibrant-williams-4b0f66).

title: Review controls: dense + LoRA-all, dense LR 1e-5 / 2e-5, sparse loss positions, random token choice
result: Dense is best at 5e-6 everywhere; random token choice nearly matches the router (+0.027 at 1,464 rows, tie at 3,904).

title: End-of-run checkpoint crash (async save on the final step overlapping teardown)
result: Fixed in 319d7442a (final-step interval save made synchronous); confirmed twice on GPU.

title: Router hill-climb round: threshold keep, MLP router, document-context features, task one-hot, per-task routers, per-group ridge, keep schedule, stage 2 at block 12, partial FFN width
result: Everything ties the linear router (0.83–0.86 vs 0.852) or loses; first stage at block 5 −0.033; 75% FFN width −0.10. A better router predicts gradients better (rank corr 0.54 vs 0.37) but does not score better.

title: Whole-model LoRA with frozen output layer: full budget curve to 960 steps
result: Never behind dense; FLOPs-to-match 4.8 / 4.3 / 3.2 / 2.1 / ≈1.4× at 48 / 120 / 240 / 480 / 960 steps; 22.3 vs 35.2 GiB peak.

title: Fresh 4-task pools (mt4f, 8,200 rows/task, generator seed 5310)
result: Built; zero train/eval overlap on nq and outlier (not checked for contradiction / oolong).

title: Rerank / reorder graders for the 11-task mix
result: Tolerant reorder and rerank graders fixed; rerank evals launched from prasann/eval-rerank-lora. Not yet on the hub's 11-task means.

title: Max trainable length at 80 GB (memory probes + four memory fixes)
result: With all fixes: dense ≈165k, 10% router ≈250k, two-stage ≈255k, 20% router ≈270k, recipe ≈300k, whole-model LoRA ≈400k tokens per row.

title: Recipe at 64k on the 11-task mix (¼ epoch, 10× data)
result: +0.037 task average over dense at matched FLOPs, ahead on all 10 graded tasks, 0.365× FLOPs, 24% less peak memory. Gains grow with length (contradiction +0.041 at 8k → +0.119 at 64k). 1 seed.

title: Wall-clock vs FLOPs analysis
result: Cheap methods run at 0.54–0.65× dense step time for 0.22–0.30× FLOPs; predicted ≈0.29–0.47× after packing, fused LoRA and compile.

title: Gradient composition probe (SFT checkpoints + CPT addendum)
result: Blocks 0–6 hold 0.45 of the parameter gradient at the base, 0.20–0.40 after training; documents dominate early-mid blocks and fade with depth; rankings decorrelate with depth (case for rescoring at block 16). CPT importance is flat (top 10% hold 0.62).

title: LoRA early stack (rank 64 on blocks 0–6, frozen base) with the router
result: Same quality as the plain router at 0.25× dense FLOPs (vs 0.30×) and 48.4 vs 60.3 GiB peak, from step 0 (2 seeds). Rank 16 worse.

title: Two-stage keep (20% after block 7, 7% after block 16)
result: Best router quality on the 1,464-row original pool (+0.11 outlier over one-stage at matched FLOPs, 2 seeds); ties one-stage on fresh pools and the 11-task mix.

title: Freeze variants: freeze blocks 0–6 at 50% / 75%, progressive freeze
result: Fine on the 4-task mix (0.21–0.24× FLOPs) but freezing costs xabsence on the 11-task mix (0.54–0.58 vs 0.68–0.71), so the recipe does not freeze.

title: Mixture-of-depths (capacity 0.25, blocks 8–30 alternate) and adaptive keep by predicted gradient mass
result: MoD loses outlier (−0.25) at 0.78× FLOPs; adaptive keep spends more FLOPs for no gain.

title: Aggressive-cut screen: no full-context steps, frozen / no-grad early stack, pyramid, merging dropped tokens, early-exit loss
result: Dropping the full-context steps is free; freezing from step 0, the pyramid and merging all lose contradiction (0.34–0.55 vs 0.66); early-exit loss is a no-op on SFT.

title: Token dropping in CPT: router, input drops, slots, MoD, all-local attention, early-exit loss, partial MLP
result: Every variant loses to dense; whole-model LoRA without dropping wins instead.

title: Split-point sweep (drop after block 1–12), router target ablation, exploration share
result: Cliff between blocks 6 and 7 (outlier 0.38 → 0.58); gradient-norm target best (residual-change target near random); exploration 0–50% all fine.

title: Gradient fidelity v1 and offline router-accuracy probe
result: Router near a perfect predictor (cos 0.78 vs 0.83 after block 7; 0.45 vs 0.50 at the input); mid-stack drop is the big lever. Router rank correlation 0.5–0.6 from block-8 features.

title: 64k study: online router (keep 10% after block 7) vs dense, ¼ to 1 epoch
result: ≈+0.03 task average over dense at matched FLOPs at every budget (≈1.6–1.7× FLOPs-to-match); trails dense by ≈0.03 on the same data. Gain grows with eval length to 16–32k and holds at 64k.

title: Fixed keep rules: gold kept whole + trimmed context, gold-blind and two-tier rules, LR sweep
result: Gold-whole rules learn a shortcut (contradiction@8k 0.03–0.07 vs dense 0.89 at every LR); gold-blind rules at best tie dense at 0.57× FLOPs.

title: Earlier compute-saving work: soft-KV, soft-token slots, routed FFN, dev-loss scheme grid
result: Superseded by the online router; pages linked in the hub's archive.
